chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Khallad al-Sindy, from Amr ibn Shimr, [from Jabir], from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'A man marries his midwife.' He said: 'No, nor her daughter.'

key_terms.قَابِلَتَهُ: his midwife (female who assists in childbirth)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry the midwife who delivered his child?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the prohibition of marrying a midwife (*qabalah*) and her daughter, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of avoiding potential conflicts of interest or undue influence during childbirth. This ruling underscores the importance of maintaining clear familial and social boundaries within the context of reproductive health and family law in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Khallad Al sindy, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man marries his midwife’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, nor her daughter’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Khalfad af-Sindiy from “Amr ibn Shamir from (Jabir) who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
if one can marry his al- Qabilah (special nurse who helps one’s mother during her giving birth and thereafter). He (the Imam) said, ‘No, and not her daughter also.’”
